title: Big Tech just delivered the most consequential earnings week of 2026
author: Sigma Capital
metaDescription: Google's parent company delivered the standout earnings result of 2026, with revenue of $107 billion and Google Cloud surpassing $20 billion for the first time.
excerpt: Google's parent company delivered the standout earnings result of 2026, with revenue of $107 billion and Google Cloud surpassing $20 billion for the first time. The Magnificent 7 tech companies significantly drove the S&P 500's blended earnings growth rate to 27.1% year-over-year.

content.introduction: Google's parent company delivered the standout earnings result of 2026, with revenue of $107 billion and Google Cloud surpassing $20 billion for the first time. The Magnificent 7 tech companies significantly drove the S&P 500's blended earnings growth rate to 27.1% year-over-year.
body: Following the busiest week of first-quarter earnings season last week, it’s the second busiest week with 128 S&P 500 companies scheduled to report. Companies reporting and combining actual results with consensus estimates for companies yet to report, the S&P 500’s blended earnings growth rate for the quarter is 27.1% year-over-year, above the 13.2% expectations at the end of the quarter. Because technology companies are critical drivers of earnings growth and account for a significant percentage of the S&P 500’s market capitalization, the Magnificent 7 remains the group to watch this earnings season. While all five reported better-than-expected earnings, investors reacted differently to the results and capital expenditure plans. Microsoft has robust growth in its cloud business (Azure), which remains capacity-constrained, but higher-than-expected capital expenditures and slightly lower-than-consensus earnings guidance for next quarter sent the stock 2.4% lower. Better-than-expected earnings reports within the communication services and consumer discretionary sectors were the primary contributors to the improvement in the blended earnings growth rate.
The cloud numbers from this week were not noise. They were the leading edge of what is going to be the most consequential enterprise technology
